The paper presents a novel design of microwave absorbers based on multilayered composite materials.
The design utilizes transmission line theory (TLT) and particle swarm optimization (PSO).
The frequency range of the designed absorber is from 2.0 to 18.0 GHz.
The minimum reflection loss of the Type-IV design is -17.75 dB at 3.26 GHz.
The total thickness of the Type-IV design is 3.00 mm.
The bandwidth of the Type-IV design is nearly 15 GHz.
The incident angle range used in the simulation is from 0° to 45° with an interval of 15°.
The material used in the matching layer of the Type-IV design is S1 (composite material with 10% CIP).
The material used in the absorbing layer of the Type-IV design is S2 (composite material with 35% CIP).
The optimization method used in the design is particle swarm optimization (PSO).
The cost function used in the optimization is f = k1·Γmin + k2∑di + k3·WB + k4·Γave.
The weight of each term in the cost function is k1, k2, k3, and k4.
The designed absorbers can cover most of the radar's frequency range.
The designed absorbers have a good performance under different incident angles and polarizations.
